result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You came to the Emergency Department after a fall at home. You hit your head. You did not lose consciousness.

- Your right hip X-ray showed no fracture.
- Your head scan (CT) showed no bleeding inside the head.
- Your blood pressure was 142/80 lying down. It was 108/66 standing up.
- This shows postural hypotension. This means your blood pressure drops when you stand up.
- Amlodipine may be making your blood pressure drop when you stand.

## What you need to do
1. Stop amlodipine 10 mg.
2. Continue all your other medicines.
3. Stand up slowly.
4. Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand.
5. Wait for the Falls Prevention Clinic to write to you with an appointment. The hospital has made the referral.

Your GP will recheck your blood pressure, lying and standing, in 4 weeks.

## Dates and medicines
- 14 October 2026: you were seen at the Emergency Department.
- In 4 weeks: your GP will recheck your lying and standing blood pressure.
- Amlodipine 10 mg: stop. It may be making your blood pressure drop when you stand.
- All other medicines: continue.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What does postural hypotension mean for me?
- Will I need a different medicine in place of amlodipine?
- When will the Falls Prevention Clinic contact me?

## When to get urgent help
If you get a worsening headache, vomiting, confusion or drowsiness in the next few days, call 999 or go to A&E (the hospital emergency department).

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
